3.4 Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
Employees are strictly prohibited from offering, giving, soliciting, or accepting bribes, kickbacks, or other improper 
payments in connection with Company business, in compliance with the U.S. Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and 
equivalent international laws.
3.5 Confidentiality and Data Protection
Employees must protect confidential Company, client, and employee information at all times, both during and after 
employment. Confidential information includes but is not limited to trade secrets, financial data, client lists, source 
code, and personnel records. Unauthorized disclosure may result in termination and legal action.

2.4 Employment of Relatives
Relatives of current employees may be hired as long as they do not directly supervise, or be supervised by, a 
relative, and do not work within the same direct reporting line. Exceptions require written approval from the Chief 
People Officer.
2.5 Background Checks and Verification
Offers of employment are contingent upon successful completion of a background check, which may include 
verification of employment history, education, criminal record checks (where legally permitted), and reference 
checks.
3. Code of Conduct and Ethics
3.1 General Standards of Conduct
Employees are expected to act with integrity, professionalism, and respect in all interactions with colleagues, clients, 
vendors, and the public. Conduct that reflects poorly on the Company, undermines trust, or violates the law is 
grounds for disciplinary action, up to and including termination.
3.2 Conflicts of Interest

Certain violations, including theft, workplace violence, harassment, falsification of records, or gross misconduct, 
may result in immediate termination without progressing through the standard disciplinary steps.
8.4 Voluntary Resignation
Employees are asked to provide a minimum of two weeks' written notice of resignation. Exit interviews are 
conducted by the People & Culture Department to gather feedback and ensure a smooth offboarding process.

7.4 Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)
Personal devices used to access Company email or systems must be enrolled in the Company's mobile device 
management (MDM) platform and comply with minimum security requirements, including passcode protection and 
remote wipe capability.
7.5 Incident Reporting
Suspected security incidents, including phishing emails, lost devices, or unauthorized access, must be reported 
immediately to the IT Security team at security@nexorasolutions.example or via the internal incident reporting tool.
7.6 Social Media and Public Communications
Employees are personally responsible for content they post on social media. Employees must not disclose 
confidential Company information and should include a disclaimer that views expressed are their own when 
discussing industry topics related to their role. Only designated spokespeople may speak on behalf of the Company 
to media outlets.

Unused PTO may be carried over up to a maximum of 5 days into the following calendar year. PTO requests should 
be submitted at least two weeks in advance through the HR portal and are subject to manager approval based on 
business needs.
4.3 Sick Leave
In addition to PTO, employees receive 8 paid sick days per calendar year for personal illness, medical appointments, 
or care of an immediate family member. A doctor's note may be required for absences exceeding 3 consecutive days.

7.3 Data Classification and Handling
Company data is classified into four tiers: Public, Internal, Confidential, and Restricted. Confidential and Restricted 
data (including client PII, financial records, and source code) must be encrypted at rest and in transit, and may only 
be accessed by authorized personnel on a need-to-know basis.

1.2 Acknowledgment of Receipt
All employees are required to read this Handbook in full and sign an acknowledgment of receipt within thirty (30) 
calendar days of their start date. Acknowledgment forms are retained in each employee's personnel file.
1.3 Policy Review and Amendments
This Handbook is reviewed annually by the People & Culture Department and Legal Department, and may be 
amended at any time at the Company's discretion. Employees will be notified of material changes via company-wide 
email and the internal policy portal.

2.1 Equal Employment Opportunity
Nexora Solutions is an equal opportunity employer. The Company prohibits discrimination and harassment of any 
kind based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, sexual

5.5 Expense Reimbursement
Employees are reimbursed for reasonable, pre-approved business expenses submitted through the expense 
management system within 30 days of the expense being incurred, accompanied by itemized receipts.
6. Workplace Health, Safety, and Conduct
6.1 Workplace Safety
Nexora is committed to providing a safe working environment in compliance with OSHA and applicable local 
regulations. Employees must report unsafe conditions, accidents, or injuries to their manager and Facilities 
immediately.

9. Business Travel Policy
9.1 Booking and Approval
All business travel must be booked through the Company's approved travel portal and pre-approved by the 
employee's manager. Airfare should be booked in economy class for flights under 6 hours and premium economy 
for longer flights, subject to budget guidelines.
9.2 Per Diem and Meal Allowances
Employees traveling on Company business receive a daily meal allowance of $75 USD domestically and $100 USD 
internationally, in lieu of itemized meal receipts.
9.3 Travel Safety
Employees traveling to regions with elevated risk advisories must register their itinerary with the Security team and 
follow all guidance issued prior to and during travel.

4.4 Holidays
Nexora observes the following paid holidays each year: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor 
Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day. Employees in other countries observe the 
statutory holiday schedule applicable to their location.
4.5 Parental and Family Leave
Eligible employees are entitled to 16 weeks of paid parental leave following the birth, adoption, or foster placement 
of a child. Leave may be taken continuously or intermittently within 12 months of the qualifying event, subject to 
manager coordination.
4.6 Bereavement Leave
Employees may take up to 5 paid days of bereavement leave for the death of an immediate family member, and up 
to 2 paid days for the death of a extended family member or close friend.

3.2 Conflicts of Interest
Employees must avoid situations in which personal interests conflict, or appear to conflict, with the interests of the 
Company. Employees must disclose any actual or potential conflict of interest to their manager and the People & 
Culture Department in writing.
1. Outside employment that competes with or interferes with Company duties.
2. Financial interests in a competitor, supplier, or client (exceeding 1% of a publicly traded company is 
exempt).
3. Accepting gifts or hospitality from vendors or clients valued above $100 USD.
4. Hiring or supervising a close family member without disclosure.
3.3 Anti-Harassment and Anti-Bullying Policy
Nexora maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward harassment, bullying, or retaliation of any kind. This includes 
verbal, physical, or visual conduct that creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work environment. Employees

2.2 Employment Classifications
• Full-Time Employee: Regularly scheduled to work at least 35 hours per week.
• Part-Time Employee: Regularly scheduled to work fewer than 35 hours per week.
• Temporary Employee: Hired for a specific project or defined period, typically not to exceed 12 months.
• Independent Contractor: Engaged under a separate contractor agreement and not subject to this Handbook 
except where explicitly stated.

4.7 Jury Duty and Voting Leave
Nexora provides paid leave for jury duty and up to 4 hours of paid leave to vote in public elections when an 
employee's work schedule does not otherwise allow sufficient time to vote.
4.8 Unpaid Leave of Absence
Employees may request an unpaid leave of absence for personal reasons not covered by other leave policies. 
Requests must be submitted in writing to the People & Culture Department at least 30 days in advance where 
possible and are granted at the Company's discretion.
5. Compensation and Benefits
5.1 Pay Schedule
Employees are paid on a bi-weekly basis, with pay periods ending every other Friday and payment issued the 
following Friday via direct deposit.
5.2 Overtime
Non-exempt employees are compensated at 1.5 times their regular hourly rate for hours worked beyond 40 in a 
workweek, in accordance with the Fair Labor Standards Act and applicable state law. Overtime must be pre-
approved by a manager.

1. Introduction and Purpose
This Employee Handbook and Company Policy Manual (the "Handbook") establishes the official policies, 
procedures, and standards of conduct for all employees of Nexora Solutions Inc. ("Nexora," "the Company," "we," 
or "us"). It is designed to provide clear guidance on expectations, benefits, and responsibilities shared between the 
Company and its employees.
This Handbook applies to all employees, regardless of position, location, or employment type, unless otherwise 
stated within a specific policy. It supersedes all previous versions of the Handbook and any verbal or informal 
statements of policy.
1.1 Purpose of This Document
This document serves as the single source of truth for company policy and is maintained for reference by employees, 
managers, and the People & Culture Department. It is also intended to serve as a knowledge base for internal 
support tools, including automated assistants that answer employee questions about policy.

3.6 Reporting Violations and Whistleblower Protection
Employees who observe conduct that violates this Handbook, the law, or Company policy should report it to their 
manager, the People & Culture Department, or through the confidential Ethics Hotline at 
ethics@nexorasolutions.example or 1-800-555-0142. Nexora strictly prohibits retaliation against any employee who 
reports a concern in good faith.
4. Attendance, Time Off, and Leave Policies
4.1 Working Hours and Attendance
Standard business hours are Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time, with a one-hour unpaid lunch 
break. Department-specific schedules may vary and will be communicated by the employee's manager. Employees 
are expected to be punctual and to notify their manager as early as possible in the event of an absence or late arrival.

5.3 Performance Reviews and Merit Increases
Formal performance reviews are conducted annually each Q1, with optional mid-year check-ins in Q3. Merit-based 
salary adjustments, where applicable, are effective April 1 of each year following the review cycle.
5.4 Health and Welfare Benefits
• Medical, dental, and vision insurance, with the Company covering 80% of employee premiums and 60% of 
dependent premiums.
• 401(k) retirement plan with a 4% Company match, fully vested after 2 years of service.
• Life insurance and short/long-term disability coverage at no cost to the employee.
• Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing free confidential counseling and support services.
• Annual wellness stipend of $500 for gym memberships, fitness equipment, or wellness apps.

8. Performance Management and Discipline
8.1 Performance Improvement Plans (PIP)
Employees whose performance falls below expectations may be placed on a Performance Improvement Plan 
outlining specific, measurable goals and a defined timeline (typically 30–90 days) for improvement, developed 
collaboratively with their manager and the People & Culture Department.
8.2 Progressive Discipline
Nexora generally follows a progressive discipline process, though the Company reserves the right to bypass steps 
depending on the severity of the conduct:
5. Verbal warning and documented coaching conversation.
6. Written warning placed in the employee's personnel file.
7. Final written warning and/or suspension, where applicable.

6.2 Remote and Hybrid Work Policy
Eligible employees may work remotely up to 3 days per week, subject to manager approval and role requirements. 
Remote employees must maintain a secure, distraction-free workspace and remain reachable during core business 
hours (10:00 AM–4:00 PM local time).
6.3 Dress Code
Nexora maintains a business-casual dress code for office-based roles. Client-facing employees should dress 
professionally on days involving client meetings. Casual attire, including jeans, is permitted on Fridays.
6.4 Drug and Alcohol Policy
Employees may not report to work or perform job duties under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs. Alcohol 
may be served in moderation at approved Company events. Employees are encouraged to seek support through the 
EAP for substance-related concerns.
6.5 Weapons and Violence Prevention
Nexora prohibits the possession of weapons on Company property and enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy toward

Nexora prohibits the possession of weapons on Company property and enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy toward 
threats or acts of violence in the workplace.
6.6 Workplace Visitors and Children
Visitors must sign in at reception and be escorted by an employee at all times. Children may visit the office briefly 
but may not be left unsupervised or brought in on a regular basis during working hours.
7. Information Technology and Data Security Policy
7.1 Acceptable Use of Company Systems
Company-provided computers, phones, email, and software are intended primarily for business use. Limited 
personal use is permitted provided it does not interfere with job performance, consume excessive resources, or 
violate any other Company policy.
7.2 Password and Account Security
• Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols.
• Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for all Company systems, including email and VPN access.
